messages:
Samir: FYI billing alarm just blew up, daily spend jumped to $74.9k from usual ~$8k. looks correlated with scale events.
Priya: omg, any immediate kill switch?
Samir: I already paused the autoscaler for the training fleet (kubectl patch) and set desired=10 for the cluster. still seeing new compute in cloud console.
Alex W: Do we have the autoscaler config that maps job labels -> instance types? last time a label typo caused t4->a100 mapping.
Samir: pulling logs now. cluster-autoscaler events show: 
```
Event: ScaleUp: requesting 40 nodes for label gpu=true -> nodeGroup: gpu-a100-group (machineType: a2-highgpu-8g, accelerator: type=nvidia-a100,count=8)
```
Samir: but our launcher is supposed to use g4dn.xlarge equivalents (cheaper). seems nodeGroup config got swapped with reserved pool.
Maya: wait reserved pool? that means the reserved capacity contract is assigned to the wrong node template and it forced launches into the 'reserved-a100' pool which is expensive and uncommitted use is billed standard rate.
InfraBot: [ALERT] billing.alerts@example.com triggered: spend rate 3.7x expected. Autoscaler activity > 300 nodes/hour for cluster-production-01.
Priya: Can someone check the min_size/max_size? If min_size was bumped it could prevent scale down.
Alex W: looking. terraform record shows: 
```
module "gpu_pool" {
  min_size = 50  # <-- oops this was copied from batch-pool
  max_size = 200
  machine_type = "a2-highgpu-8g"
}
```
Alex W: that min_size is wrong for production serving; should be 5. That explains runaway baseline.
Samir: gah, a copy-paste error and an incorrect nodeGroup name mapping. So two failure modes: min_size locked upscale and wrong machine_type causing cost per node to be 6-8x.
OpsLead: Good catch. Immediate plan: 1) reduce min_size to 5 2) replace machine_type in nodeGroup to g4dn.xlarge 3) revoke autoscaler permission to attach reserved-a100 pool 4) open incident ticket and notify finance.
Priya: I'm on (1) & (2) now. Making a small tf change and will run plan/app. tagging @Alex W for review.
Samir: finance said current spike already consumed $180k of on-demand that would have been covered by our reserved commitment in us-central — because templates launched in us-east and owned pool not recognized by commitment.
Maya: so region mismatch too. We need a quick script to detect node launches outside committed regions and kill them. I can hack one in 20m.
InfraBot: [ACTION] autoscaler:pause applied by Samir at 2024-09-15T16:12Z
Alex W: PR open: changed min_size and node template; also added validation to prevent machine_type values that include "a2-" unless explicitly allowed. also added unit test for terraform module.
Samir: after pause + tf apply we scaled down from 180 -> 12 nodes over 30m. billing rate trending back down but finance wants postmortem and cost recovery plan.
Priya: postmortem outline: timeline, root causes (tf copy, nodeGroup mapping, region mismatch), blast radius, dollars, short-term mitigation, long-term controls (policy guardrails, pre-deploy validator, autoscaler runaway alert), owners.
OpsLead: Assigning owners: Priya -> immediate fixes and postmortem, Maya -> region detector script, Alex W -> terraform validation & unit tests, Samir -> communication with finance and customers. Target postmortem draft EOD.
Maya: also recommended: add a soft budget limit that triggers autoscaler:force-scale-to=baseline and notifies SRE on-call.
Samir: agree. Follow-ups: add a cost-alert that ties to autoscaler churn, add an infra-policy that forbids reserved-pool mapping mismatches, and run a one-off audit of all nodeGroups for region and machine_type correctness.
Priya: thanks all. filing the incident ticket and pinging finance + cs. :white_check_mark:
Alex W: learned: be suspicious of copy/paste in tf modules. Also we need a canary step when altering node templates in prod.
Samir: closing thread as we have autoscaler paused and tf fixes in flight. Will update ticket with numbers when billing clears.
